title: The Four Elements in the Body: Stripping the Defiled Garments and the Two Endings
arc: The teaching follows the four elements from their pure origin in luminaries and saints, through their mingling with darkness and their binding into bodies on the Cross of Light, where they shed a graded series of "defiled garments" — and ends by dividing two destinies: those that are purified in the New Man and ascend to first rest, and those that multiply sin and pass into metensomatosis under judgment.
reading:
This chapter answers the question implied in its heading: why were the four elements ever placed into bodies and bound to the Cross of Light? The answer is given as a single spiritual movement that begins before the cosmos, runs through the body's entire life as a battlefield of stripping, and ends in one of two outcomes — ascent to the Land of the Living or descent into transmigration under sentence.

The teaching opens by reminding the chosen one that these four elements are "from the beginning." In themselves they belong to the holy and the living; they are the substance of the luminaries, the Five Sons of the First Man as the Living Soul dispersed in nature. They are not evil. But "in that first contest" — the primal war — Error and the Darkness of the Enemy mingled with them. From that mingling onward the elements no longer exist in pure form: they exist as Living Soul bound in bodies, which is precisely what the Cross of Light names. The body, then, is not first of all a prison; it is the appointed working-place where the elements, having been mingled, can be sorted.

The middle of the teaching — its longest stretch — describes that sorting as a cascade of strippings. When the elements come into a body, they "leave naked the defiled garments and abandon them in the flesh." These cast-off garments are not neutral residue; they re-emerge and become a danger to the body itself. The teaching then traces the strippings as a hierarchy, each layer revealing the next more interior falsity-from-evil beneath it. The bond, when stripped, exposes wrath; wrath, when stripped, exposes the flowing torrent by which the counsels themselves strip themselves bare — that is desire (epithymia); desire stripped exposes bitterness, the very taste of falsity-from-evil; bitterness stripped exposes heat; and beyond that the light's own stripping reaches the flesh itself, which when stripped exposes gloom, and gloom severity. These are then identified with what the tree (the corrupt perception, the Bitter Tree) strips off as "winds of shame" — disordered perceptions of corrupt affection — and finally the whole series is summed under the figure of twelve strippings, a complete circuit corresponding to the zodiacal totality of natural states. The four elements are the agents that effect this whole graded undressing in the body's economy of psychic food: as they pass inward through eating, breathing, and sensation, they peel away layer after layer of the mingled darkness that had clothed them, exposing each interior falsity until only the living substance remains.

This is why the elements were put into bodies: the body is the working-loom of separation. Without descent into flesh, the mingled light cannot be uncovered layer by layer. The Cross of Light is the form of this redemptive suffering — Divine Truth dispersed and crucified in the natural so that, through the body's ordered processes, it can be successively stripped of every defiled garment from outermost wrath down to inmost severity.

The arc closes with the two endings. When the elements come into a body that is being regenerated, they are chosen, purified, and "stand fast in their living icon, which is the New Man"; they receive the Mind of Light, are purified within that icon, and come forth chosen and holy, reaching their "first rest" — the threshold of ascent to the Country of the Living Ones along the Pillar of Glory. But when the same elements come into the body of sinners, the defilements that should have been stripped instead multiply within; the soul confirms itself in sins, and its end is metensomatosis — being passed from body to body — together with a sentence. The same four elements, the same Cross of Light, the same descent into flesh: the difference is whether the icon worn within is the New Man or the proprium, whether the strippings are received or resisted.

Thus the whole teaching is a single argument: the elements were put into bodies because only embodied life provides the graded resistance through which the mingled light can be progressively unclothed of darkness. The body bound to the Cross of Light is the necessary instrument of redemption — and the same instrument that, refused, becomes the wheel of judgment.
